details.label: Discussion
details.text: Multiple pulse cellular storms and multicellular clusters have intensified over the past couple of hours as they attempt to approach the lower terrain from the Mogollon Rim. As this occurs, the storms will overspread a hot boundary layer, characterized by surface temperatures over 100 F amid mid 50s F dewpoints. Ample evaporative cooling potential exists, as shown by 22Z mesoanalysis, with 1500-2000 J/kg DCAPE in place. As such, despite weaker vertical wind shear, a couple of the stronger storm cores may produce dry downbursts capable of supporting severe gusts through the afternoon and evening hours. Nonetheless, the severe threat should stay somewhat sparse, precluding the need of a WW issuance. ..Squitieri/Mosier.. 08/08/2026 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A band of convection with a history of wind damage continues to move east across the New England region. Although the band has taken on a somewhat more pronounced bowing structure, latest radar imagery from KBOX shows the emergence of an outflow boundary on the southern flank of the line. This hints at some degree of weakening. However, surface observations downstream continue to show a warm and moist air mass in place that is supporting a pocket of MLCAPE between 1500-2000 J/kg. Additionally, the KBOX VWP is sampling 30-50 knot flow between 5-7 km AGL, which is yielding stronger deep-layer bulk shear than depicted by recent mesoanalyses. Consequently, is seems probable that this line will maintain some degree of intensity (especially on the northern flank) as it moves into eastern MA over the next 1-2 hours with some threat for damaging/severe winds (most likely peak gusts in the 45-60 mph range based on recent observations and the downstream environment). ..Moore.. 08/08/2026 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms have been slowly intensifying along the Appalachians over the past 2-3 hours per regional radar imagery and lightning trends. More recently, much of this activity has exhibited strong outflow - a manifestation of the poor kinematic environment (also confirmed by regional VWPs). Furthermore, west/southwesterly mid-level flow is favoring storm motions along the zone of ascent, which is limiting southeastward propagation into a more deeply-mixed and buoyant air mass (characterized by 0-3 km lapse rates near 8 C/km and around 1000 J/kg MLCAPE). Nonetheless, some degree of storm propagation into the well-mixed/buoyant air is probable as outflows surge south/southeastward and collide. Convection developing within this regime will be capable of produce strong downbursts with embedded swaths of damaging winds (most likely 45-60 mph). Confidence in the coverage and/or duration of intense convection is very limited and precludes watch issuance, but a few instances of wind damage appear possible over the next couple of hours prior to the onset of nocturnal cooling after 00 UTC. ..Moore/Mosier.. 08/08/2026 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has been slowly intensifying along a diffuse cold front from the northern shores of Lake Erie southwestward into western OH. So far most of this convection has largely been shallow with only occasional updraft pulses strong enough to produce lightning. However, with time the expectation is that continued forcing along the approaching front, combined with gradually deepening cold pools (especially where storm clustering can occur), should support adequate lift for intensification of a few cells/clusters within an otherwise buoyant and weakly capped environment. Regional VWPs are sampling mid-level winds between 30-35 knots, which should yield effective bulk shear values of around 25 knots - sufficient for some degree of storm organization. Consequently, a severe storm or two capable of producing damaging gusts and perhaps small to marginally severe hail may emerge from this regime over the next couple of hours. In general, the weak forcing for ascent should limit the coverage of strong/severe storms, and the onset of nocturnal cooling after 00 UTC should temporally constrain the severe threat to the next few hours. Given these limitations, watch issuance appears unlikely. ..Moore/Mosier.. 08/08/2026 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A lone multicellular cluster has matured over northern KS in the past hour, likely driven by the intersection of a strongly heated/mixed boundary layer and weak surface convergence along a baroclinic boundary. A belt of 15-20 kt southerly low-level flow is in place across the Plains, overspread by 30+ kt 500 mb northwesterlies, resulting in 40+ kts of effective bulk shear over northern KS. The baroclinic boundary precedes the ongoing multicellular cluster, where surface dewpoints exceed 70 F, yielding over 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Nonetheless, forcing for ascent is weak in this region, casting great uncertainty on the coverage and overall longevity of any severe threat. Current visible satellite does not suggest any imminent threat for additional convective development in the near term. Still, given adequate vertical wind shear and instability, a conditional threat for a few severe gusts and perhaps an instance of severe hail may accompany this multicellular cluster, assuming it persists along the baroclinic boundary. ..Squitieri/Mosier.. 08/08/2026 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
